notes: YOUR BACKUPS SHOULD SURVIVE THE COMPUTER THEY ARE TAKEN ON. A backup folder on this same machine used to be reported as healthy for ever. It is not a backup: one theft, one dead disk, and the ledger and every copy of it go together. This release checks whether the folder you chose actually survives this computer — a cloud folder such as OneDrive, or a separate drive — and says plainly when it does not, instead of showing a reassuring tick. GOING LIVE NOW ASKS FOR A BACKUP DESTINATION. Once, at the moment the books start to matter. Setting up and testing in UAT is deliberately untouched. AUTOMATIC BACKUPS NOW RUN HOURLY, NOT ONLY AT SIGN-IN. An office that leaves the program open all week was getting one backup attempt, on Monday morning, with nothing but a quiet notice to say so. A CLOUD FOLDER WITH NO PASSPHRASE means the full ledger — salaries included — sits readable in that cloud account. That is now a warning that stays on screen until a passphrase is set, rather than a notice that can be missed. PRINT A BACKUP RECOVERY SHEET. Backup & Export → Print recovery sheet gives you one page carrying everything the person restoring the books will need: where the backups are kept, the steps to restore them, and the organisation name the restore is checked against — with a ruled line to write the passphrase on BY HAND. It deliberately never prints the passphrase itself: a print dialogue offers Save as PDF, and that file's likeliest home is the same cloud folder as the backups. Keep the sheet where the books' owner can reach it and no one else can. ALSO. Trial and licence messages now name the dates they refer to, and a licence file that cannot be read says exactly that instead of claiming an evaluation has ended. There is NO database change in this release: your data and settings are untouched, and the upgrade is simply installing over the old version.
